name: MCP Connector for wp2ai – Control Center for ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini
author: webNdev

sections.description:
wp2ai is a WordPress MCP server that protects your sites from AI mistakes. Connect ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini through the Model Context Protocol (MCP): your AI publishes and edits your content, while wp2ai checks changes before they go live, audits your existing content and keeps a history of every action you can roll back in one click.

  • Publish directly to WordPress from your AI conversation
  • Edit existing content by replacing it in place, without touching the rest, on Gutenberg, Elementor, Bricks and Classic Editor. Insert blocks on Gutenberg and Classic Editor, and move them on Gutenberg.
  • From the Solo plan, any change to published content waits for your approval by default, publishing a draft included, with a detailed analysis and one-click undo. Drafts remain freely editable, and automatic mode can be turned on site by site.
  • From the Solo plan, validation rules check each change before it is applied: 12 rules on structure and completeness, 30 rules including SEO and quality from the Pro plan.
  • Simulate a publication before sending it, on the rules of your plan (12 on Solo, all 30 from Pro): wp2ai checks the site policies, analyses the content and the post state, without publishing anything, and returns a precise result with a suggested fix.
  • Configure global and per-site editorial instructions (tone, structure, length), sent automatically to your AI at the start of every session.
  • From the Pro plan, spot internal linking opportunities and broken links directly in the conversation with your AI.
  • Track the health score of each article: structure and completeness from the Solo plan, plus quality and SEO from the Pro plan.
  • Set protection rules per site: draft-only publishing, daily action limits, deletion blocking.
  • From the Pro plan, follow all your sites in one multi-site view, and work as a team with rights per user and per site on the Agency plan.

Compatibility

  • Page builders and editors: Gutenberg, Classic Editor, Elementor (including the Atomic Editor) and Bricks
  • SEO plugins: wp2ai reads and writes SEO titles and meta descriptions in Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, All in One SEO (4.9.8 and later) and Squirrly SEO (14.2.7 and later), always in the SEO plugin active on your site.

What the plugin does

  • Connects your site to wp2ai in one click, no API key to copy or store
  • Your AI reads your content and proposes real edits, using the same block structure your editor already uses
  • From the Solo plan, every change to published content waits for your approval by default and becomes a WordPress revision you can approve or cancel. Nothing goes live without your consent unless you turn on automatic mode.
  • From the Solo plan, a complete history of every action, so you always know what changed and can revert it in one click.

Service relationship

wp2ai is a hosted service, an account is required. The plugin on its own does not provide any AI functionality: it is the connector between your site and this service through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). See the External services section below for the exact detail of what is sent, and where.

Freemium and Premium

Create an account and enjoy a 14 day Pro trial, no credit card required (pre-publish simulation, smart internal linking, full quality score, and more). Once the trial ends, you automatically switch to the Free plan, or move to a paid plan. The Free plan gives MCP access with 20 actions per month, without validation rules, approval or action history.

Source code

The plugin ships as plain PHP with no build step and no minified assets: the code in the distributed ZIP is the complete, human-readable source.

External services

This plugin connects to the wp2ai service, operated by webNdev. The connection is not automatic: nothing is sent until an administrator explicitly starts the pairing flow from the plugin page, and everything stops when the site is disconnected.

wp2ai API

The plugin calls the wp2ai API, at https://api.wp2ai.app/functions/v1. It is contacted in these cases:

  • When you connect the site. Sends the pairing code and pairing state returned by app.wp2ai.io, your site name, your WordPress version, the plugin version and your site’s time zone (the WordPress setting, so that publications can be scheduled at the right time from the start), in order to finalize pairing and obtain connector credentials.
  • When a post is created, updated or deleted. Sends the connector identifier, a SHA-256 hash of the connector secret, the post ID and the event type, so the service knows the post needs to be re-read.
  • When content is synced. Sends, with the connector identifier and secret hash, the content of each post in scope (text, title, slug, excerpt), its metadata (ID, status, type, dates, language, featured image, SEO title and description), and structural information used for analysis and targeted edits. Also sends the site’s settings needed by the service: SEO plugin settings and related WordPress settings, site name, language and icon, the site’s time zone (the WordPress setting, used to schedule publications at the right time), and the plugin and WordPress versions. If an SEO plugin cannot be read, a technical error report is added (SEO plugin name and version, affected posts and field, error details), cleaned of the affected post’s title and slug, email addresses and absolute server paths.
  • When published pages are read. Sends, with the connector identifier and secret hash, the SEO title, meta description, canonical URL and robots directives found on each published page. Also sends what the page shows between its header and footer, so that image and call-to-action checks reflect the page as visitors see it: whether an image or a video is displayed, the text of its buttons and the presence of its forms (search forms excluded), and the identifiers (id) of the page’s elements, used to check that anchor links point to an existing part of the page. If a page cannot be read, the plugin reports it with the cause: an error code (such as a timeout, an HTTP status or a maintenance page) and a technical message, without any content of the page.
  • When the plugin polls for pending work. Sends the connector identifier and secret hash to retrieve the actions the service wants applied, and reports back whether each action succeeded or failed, with any error message, and the plugin and WordPress versions and the site’s time zone. When a full synchronization leaves posts out because their content could not be read, the report gives their number, their IDs and a technical cause for each, cleaned of the affected post’s title and slug, email addresses and absolute server paths.
  • When a template, menu, widget area, Customizer setting or theme changes. Templates are those of the page builders and of block themes (Elementor and Elementor Pro templates, Bricks templates, block theme templates and template parts, synced patterns, navigation menus). Sends, with the connector identifier and secret hash, for each change: the item’s identifier, type, slug, status and template type, its display conditions as stored by the page builder, the actions that happened (created, updated, trashed, deleted, display conditions changed, theme switched or updated), how many changes there were and the dates of the first and last one. For a theme switch, the previous and new theme names, and for a theme update whether it is the active theme. Changes are grouped and sent once the item has stayed unchanged for a minute, so that the service can check again the pages that use it.
  • When a request to analyze a content again could not be delivered. The plugin retries it, and after five failed attempts reports it with the connector identifier and secret hash: the content ID, the request identifier, the kind of change, whether the content needed to be read again, the cause, the number of attempts, the dates and the last error received (HTTP status, error code and message).
  • When you disconnect the site. Sends the connector identifier and secret hash so the service can revoke the connection.

When a post, page or draft is saved, moved to the trash or restored from it, or when its categories, tags, featured image or SEO title, description, canonical URL or robots settings change, the plugin notifies wp2ai with the content ID so that the content can be analyzed again. This notification is sent from your server to the wp2ai API (api.wp2ai.app) and contains no content: only that identifier, your site’s connector credentials, and technical fields stating the kind of change and whether the content needs to be read again.

If WooCommerce is active, the content data sent during synchronization also states whether a page is the shop, cart, checkout or account page, so that these pages are analyzed appropriately.

When wp2ai writes an SEO title or description on a site using Squirrly SEO, the plugin goes through Squirrly SEO’s own programming interface, which only accepts writes from a user allowed to edit the content. For that one call, the plugin acts with the permissions of a site administrator, then returns to the previous user. Nothing more is sent to wp2ai.

No visitor data, no site user accounts and no administrator email addresses are sent.

app.wp2ai.io

Clicking “Connect my site” opens https://app.wp2ai.io in your browser so you can sign in to your wp2ai account and authorize the site. This is a redirect in your own browser, not a server-side call: WordPress sends nothing to app.wp2ai.io by itself. app.wp2ai.io then returns you to the plugin page with the pairing code that the plugin exchanges against the API.

Terms of service: https://wp2ai.io/terms
Privacy policy: https://wp2ai.io/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to the wp2ai menu entry in the WordPress admin.
  3. Click “Connect my site”. You are sent to app.wp2ai.io to sign in and authorize the site.
  4. You are returned to the plugin page and the connection is finalized automatically.

To stop the connection, click Disconnect on the same page. The plugin notifies the service and removes the stored credentials.
sections.faq:
What is wp2ai?

wp2ai is a WordPress MCP server that protects your sites from AI mistakes. ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini publish and edit your content, while wp2ai checks changes before they go live, audits your existing content and keeps a history of every action you can roll back in one click.

Is a wp2ai account required?

Yes. The plugin is a connector to the hosted wp2ai service, and does nothing on its own without an account.

Which AI assistants are compatible?

Any tool that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP): ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and any future ones. wp2ai is not tied to any specific assistant, you use the one you already have.

Are my existing WordPress sites compatible?

Yes, from WordPress 6.0. The plugin installs in two minutes without modifying your theme or your other plugins. Compatible with Gutenberg, Elementor, Bricks and Classic Editor.

Can wp2ai edit content that is already published?

Yes. Your AI locates a specific block on an already published page and edits it without touching the rest. A WordPress revision is created before each edit. From the Solo plan, you approve each edit before it is applied, unless you turn on automatic mode for that site.

Does the plugin send my content to a third party?

It sends the content and metadata of your posts to the wp2ai service, only after an administrator has explicitly connected the site. The External services section lists every field involved. Nothing is sent before pairing, or after disconnection.

Can an AI publish to my site without my consent?

Content proposed through an AI call is sanitized before being stored, and applied actions are recorded. From the Solo plan, every change to published content, publishing included, waits for your explicit approval by default and can be undone in one click. On the Free plan, actions are applied directly.

What happens to my data if I uninstall the plugin?

Uninstalling removes the connector credentials and the plugin options stored on the site. Data already held by the wp2ai service remains managed from your wp2ai account.
sections.changelog:
0.6.140

  • New: Squirrly SEO compatibility
  • New: SEO corrections from AI assistants are saved in all compatible SEO plugins
  • New: pages are automatically rechecked when a template, menu or theme changes
  • Fixed: site connection reliability
  • Improved: images, buttons and anchor links are checked on Elementor pages and templates
  • Improved: more reliable updates on slow hosting
  • Improved: the plugin is now available in French

0.6.139

  • New: image, call to action and anchor link alerts now reflect what visitors actually see on the page
  • Improved: scheduled publications follow your site’s time zone
  • Improved: content from shortcodes and third-party blocks is now analyzed
  • Improved: undoing a change made by your AI assistant also restores its SEO title and description
  • Improved: a change that would break the page layout is refused with a clear message
  • Improved: the plugin page shows how many items could not be synced

0.6.138

  • New: your edits in WordPress, drafts included, are now checked automatically
  • Improved: every save is taken into account, even several in quick succession
  • Improved: content changes made by your AI assistant can always be undone
  • Improved: faster saves on LiteSpeed hosting

0.6.137

  • Improved: full compatibility with Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress and All in One SEO, SEO titles, descriptions and title separators match what each page displays
  • Improved: drafts get the same SEO titles and descriptions as published content
  • Improved: after a temporary interruption of the connection between the site and wp2ai, sync, change notifications and plugin disconnection resume automatically

0.6.136

  • New: the plugin page shows the date and any error from the last full sync
  • Improved: sync error messages now make it easier to identify the cause of a failure

0.6.135

  • Fixed: SEO titles and descriptions managed by Rank Math are correctly recognised as custom or auto-generated
  • Fixed: Rank Math title separators display properly

0.6.134

  • Improved: editing a page no longer delays the next full site sync

0.6.133

  • New: each page now reports a content-reading confidence level
  • Improved: full content analysis support for pages built with Bricks and with Elementor’s Atomic Editor
  • Improved: internal and external links, and images, are now analyzed on all Elementor pages
  • Improved: calls to action and Bricks headers/footers are now analyzed
  • Improved: archive pages built with Elementor’s Atomic Editor are now analyzed
  • Improved: calls to action and images inside components and reusable templates are now detected
  • Improved: Elementor Pro forms are now included in content analysis
  • Improved: headings, paragraphs, links and buttons built with Elementor’s Atomic Editor can now be edited by wp2ai
  • Improved: Bricks pages can now be edited by wp2ai, with the rest of the page kept exactly as built
  • Improved: scripts and embeds placed on an Elementor page stay exactly as they are when wp2ai edits another part of it
  • Fixed: nested accordions, icon lists, and headings using global widgets are now included in content analysis
  • Fixed: images used in Bricks layouts are now correctly recognized as in use
  • Fixed: accented and other special characters are now preserved correctly when applying content corrections

0.6.132

  • Initial release.
